CVE-2026-102631.title: authd: Account takeover via username fallback in identity matching after IdP email reassignment
CVE-2026-102631.description: In authd before 0.7.1, the user identity matching in UpdateUser (internal/users/manager.go) resolves an incoming login by the broker-scoped provider ID, but falls back to matching the username when the provider ID does not belong to any known user, and does not reject a conflicting non-empty provider ID. If an identity provider reassigns an email address, which authd uses as the username, to a new account, the new account inherits the previous user's local UID and home directory on its next login. This allows the new user to access and modify files belonging to the previous user, including credentials such as SSH keys and cloud API tokens, and silently rebinds the local account record to the new identity. As a mitigation, administrators should lock or delete the previous user's local authd account when the corresponding IdP account is removed.

CVE-2026-110676.title: Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by encoding exponent notation as full decimal digits under allow_bignum
CVE-2026-110676.description:
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by encoding exponent notation as full decimal digits under allow_bignum.

With allow_bignum, a JSON number with a fraction or exponent decodes to a Math::BigFloat, which stores the exponent separately and so decodes cheaply. Encoding it untyped or as JSON_TYPE_FLOAT writes the plain decimal form with one digit per unit of exponent. Nothing bounds the exponent, so the 12-byte text [1e30000000] encodes to 30 MB.

Untrusted JSON decoded with allow_bignum and encoded again can exhaust memory and CPU.

CVE-2026-110975.title: Autotune: kruize/autotune: kruize/autotune: datasources credential disclosure
CVE-2026-110975.description: A flaw was found in Kruize Autotune. Its REST API ships without an authentication layer, and the endpoints that return datasource configuration — the list-datasources endpoint (GET /datasources) and the datasource-metadata endpoint — serialized datasource objects using a default Gson configuration with no field-exclusion strategy. As a result, the authentication secrets stored for each configured monitoring datasource (basic-auth passwords, bearer tokens, API keys, and OAuth2 client secrets) were returned in cleartext to any client able to reach the service. An attacker with network access to Autotune could harvest these credentials and reuse them to authenticate to the backing monitoring stack.

CVE-2026-19735.title: Predictable TCP initial sequence numbers when the RFC 6528 secret key generation fails silently in the Zephyr TCP stack
CVE-2026-19735.description:
The RFC 6528 initial-sequence-number implementation in subsys/net/ip/tcp.c derived every TCP ISN from SHA-256(unique_key || four-tuple) plus a uptime-derived offset, where unique_key is a 128-bit secret filled once by sys_csrand_get(). The return value of that call was discarded and the once guard was latched to true even when the call failed. Because sys_csrand_get() leaves the destination buffer untouched on failure (it deliberately propagates the entropy-driver error rather than filling the buffer), a single failed call left unique_key as its all-zero BSS content for the remainder of the boot, with no retry, no log message and no fallback.

A failure of the cryptographic random source is required to reach the weak state — for example -ENODEV/-EIO from the entropy driver in subsys/random/random_entropy_device.c (the in-tree comment notes that the hardware RNG "might still be gathering entropy during early boot situations"), or psa_generate_random() failing in…

CVE-2026-56837.description: PraisonAI is a multi-agent teams system. From version 4.6.56 to before version 4.6.59, PraisonAI's LinearBot starts a public webhook listener on 0.0.0.0 and treats LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET as optional. An unauthenticated network caller who can reach the webhook endpoint can submit a forged Linear-Event: AgentSession request. CVE-2026-98413.title: selinux: always fill AVC decision in avc_has_perm_noaudit()
CVE-2026-98413.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

selinux: always fill AVC decision in avc_has_perm_noaudit()

avc_has_perm_noaudit() is documented to return a copy of the access
decision in @avd, but its early return for an empty requested permission
set leaves the buffer untouched. All callers pass an uninitialized
stack variable and afterwards feed it to avc_audit(), and the inode hook
even stores it in the per-task decision cache.

Fill in a deny-all, audit-all decision, similar to avd_init(), so every
caller receives a defined value at no cost on the hot path.

CVE-2026-98538.title: writeback: bound cleanup_offline_cgwb() rescans by rotating scanned inodes
CVE-2026-98538.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

writeback: bound cleanup_offline_cgwb() rescans by rotating scanned inodes

cleanup_offline_cgwb() prepares at most WB_MAX_INODES_PER_ISW inodes
per call and is called again until the dying wb is drained, but every
call walks wb->b_attached and then wb->b_dirty_time from the same end.
Inodes already prepared (they stay on the list with I_WB_SWITCH set
until the switch worker runs) and inodes that cannot be switched
(I_FREEING, I_WILL_FREE, !SB_ACTIVE, DAX, already on the target wb)
stay where they are, so each pass rescans a growing run of them under
wb->list_lock and a full drain is quadratic in the number of inodes on
the list. With ~17M inodes attached to one dying cgwb we saw this end
in soft lockups, with CPUs reported stuck for 21-48s.

Walk both lists from the oldest end and move every scanned inode to
the newest end, so the next pass starts where the previous one stopped
and the drain becomes linear.…

CVE-2026-98620.title: net: ethernet: mtk_eth_soc: unregister net_devices in case of probe failure
CVE-2026-98620.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: ethernet: mtk_eth_soc: unregister net_devices in case of probe failure

If register_netdev() fails for one of the MTK_MAX_DEVS devices in
mtk_probe(), the error path jumps to err_deinit_ppe, skipping
mtk_unreg_dev(). The previously registered net_devices are then freed by
mtk_free_dev() while still in NETREG_REGISTERED state, hitting the
BUG_ON(dev->reg_state != NETREG_UNREGISTERED).

Route the register_netdev() failure to err_unreg_netdev so the net_devices
registered so far are properly unregistered before being freed.

CVE-2026-98787.title: bpf: Fix missing migration protection in __rhtab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch()
CVE-2026-98787.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Fix missing migration protection in __rhtab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch()

bpf_mem_cache_free_rcu() uses this_cpu_ptr() which requires migration
to be disabled. All callers of rhtab_delete_elem() disable migration
except __rhtab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch(), which calls it under
rcu_read_lock() only.

On CONFIG_PREEMPT_RCU, rcu_read_lock() does not disable preemption or
migration, so the task can migrate between CPUs during the delete loop,
causing this_cpu_ptr() to trigger:

BUG: using smp_processor_id() in preemptible [00000000] code

Fix by wrapping the delete loop in migrate_disable()/migrate_enable()
in __rhtab_map_lookup_and_delete_batch(), matching the migration
protection that the other callers already provide.

CVE-2026-98880.title: ntfs3: handle set_blocksize failures
CVE-2026-98880.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs3: handle set_blocksize failures

ntfs3 uses buffer_heads, which don't handle block size > PAGE_SIZE well.
Without this, mounting we will hit the

BUG_ON(offset >= folio_size(folio));

in folio_set_bh on the first __bread_gfp call.

CVE-2026-98967.title: cxgb4/ch_ktls: disable softirqs around tid_list erases
CVE-2026-98967.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cxgb4/ch_ktls: disable softirqs around tid_list erases

chcr_ktls_cpl_act_open_rpl() inserts into tid_list from the receive path
using xa_insert_bh(). The array is shared by the adapter's connections
and initialized with XA_FLAGS_LOCK_BH. However, chcr_ktls_dev_del() and
the chcr_ktls_dev_add() error path use xa_erase(), which takes the XArray
lock without disabling softirqs.

When cleanup runs with softirqs enabled, a receive softirq for another
connection on the same CPU can interrupt the erase and spin on the lock
held by the interrupted task. Use xa_erase_bh() at both sites to match
the insertion path.

CVE-2026-99061.title: wifi: brcmfmac: fix P2P device removal race in brcmf_detach()
CVE-2026-99061.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: brcmfmac: fix P2P device removal race in brcmf_detach()

When the driver is removed while the user space process that created
the P2P device (e.g. wpa_supplicant) is still exiting, the P2P device
interface is removed twice and the kernel crashes.

The two paths are:

- wpa_supplicant, on exit, sends NL80211_CMD_DEL_INTERFACE for the P2P
device. nl80211_del_interface() holds RTNL and the wiphy mutex and
calls brcmf_p2p_del_vif(), which disables discovery and waits up to
1.5 s for BRCMF_E_IF_DEL. Then it calls brcmf_remove_interface(),
which unregisters the wdev and frees the vif and the ifp.

- brcmf_detach() sets the bus down, so BRCMF_E_IF_DEL never arrives,
and calls brcmf_remove_interface(ifp, false) for the same ifp.
brcmf_p2p_ifp_removed() reads ifp->vif and then blocks on
rtnl_lock(). When brcmf_p2p_del_vif() releases RTNL, it calls
cfg80211_unregister_wdev() on the wdev that was already unregistered
and…
